LESSON: HUMAN EXCRETORY SYSTEM

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 3.2: Human Excretory System
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human Excretory System, part of Living Things and their Environment in Grade 7 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: What is the role of the excretory system? 2. How can a healthy excretory system be maintained?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use a hand lens to observe the external parts of the skin (hair and sweat pores),

2. use a chart or model to discuss on parts and functions of the human skin ,

3. search for information on the waste products excreted through the skin (excess salts and water in sweat), lungs (carbon IV oxide), and kidneys (excess salts and water in urine),

4. discuss parts of the urinary system,

5. use locally available materials to model the urinary system,

6. use charts/ models/ animations to discuss the external parts and functions of the human kidney,

7. use print and non-print materials to search for information on the causes and prevention of kidney disorders, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use a hand lens to observe the external parts of the skin (hair and sweat pores),
2. use a chart or model to discuss on parts and functions of the human skin ,
3. search for information on the waste products excreted through the skin (excess salts and water in sweat), lungs (carbon IV oxide), and kidneys (excess salts and water in urine),
4. discuss parts of the urinary system,
5. use locally available materials to model the urinary system,
6. use charts/ models/ animations to discuss the external parts and functions of the human kidney,
7. use print and non-print materials to search for information on the causes and prevention of kidney disorders, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human Excretory System together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires speaking and listening skills as they discuss parts of the urinary

system.

● Self-efficacy: the learner develops confidence as they search for information on healthy lifestyles that promote kidney and

skin health.

Values:
● Love: the learner appreciates and embraces their natural skin as they develop and maintain a daily log of activities that

promote skin and kidney health.

● Unity: the learner works collaboratively and harmoniously with peers as they develop a daily log of activities that promote

skin and kidney health.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Health Promotion Issues: the learner learns how to improve skin and kidney health as they develop a daily log of activities that

promote skin and kidney health.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the content on healthy lifestyles that promote kidney and skin health linked to nutrition for healthy skin

and kidneys in Agriculture.
